_about: Quiz question and hints for each checklist point of the cherry-wilkes scenario, keyed by checklist point id. Used by cherry-docs.ps1. Quiz types: choice (circle a, b or c), tf (true or false), write (write a word). A point with parts has one line per part.

listen.q: Cherry says the crystal ________ is missing from her shelf.

touch.q: How does Cherry like to be comforted when she is upset?
options: someone holding her hand, if they ask first

esteem.q: Saying "You did the right thing telling me" helps build Cherry's confidence.

options: "That sounds really hard. It meant a lot to you."

positive.q: Write one positive, supportive thing the support worker said to Cherry today.
positive.key: Any warm, hopeful words, for example "We can work this out together."

prefs.q: Cherry's social, cultural and spiritual life. Fill in the gaps.

parts.q: Social: Cherry's friend from the church choir is called ________.
Cultural: Cherry says her family is an ordinary ________ family.
Spiritual: Cherry's Minister is called Reverend ________.

respect.q: Cherry's faith is important to her, so the support worker helps her see the Minister.

needs.q: Cherry's hands are weak and shaky. What can the support worker do?
options: Offer to press the phone buttons while she talks.

money.q: Cherry thinks her sister ________ is selling the ornaments to pay for her ________ shopping.

unmet.q: Which need is not being met today?
options: Cherry has not eaten breakfast or slept.

selfdet.q: The support worker should decide for Cherry what to do about Donna.

options: "I'll sort it all out for you."
"What would you like to happen, Cherry?"

risk.q: Cherry does not want to talk to Donna or the police today. She has the right to make that choice.

privacy.q: Cherry says "Please don't say anything." Who does the support worker tell?

duty.q: The support worker can promise Cherry to keep the missing ornaments a secret.

services.q: The Minister and the support service. Fill in the gaps.

parts.q: Minister: Cherry's appointment with Reverend Hill is tomorrow at ________ o'clock.
Support service: the name of the service the class gave Cherry: ________
parts.key: OPAN (Older Persons Advocacy Network), or another suitable service the class used

parts.q: Phone: the number the class helped Cherry dial: ________

selfmanage.q: Cherry talks to the Minister herself. The support worker only helps with the buttons.

strengths.q: Name one of Cherry's strengths or talents: ________
strengths.key: Any strength Cherry names: singing in the choir, knowing the story of every ornament, her faith

selfcare.q: What can Cherry still do for herself?

values.q: If the support worker thinks Donna is wrong, they should tell Cherry what to do about her sister.

physical.q: Cherry's shaky hands make it hard for her to use the phone. Her physical situation affects her wellbeing.

variation.q: Cherry is still in her dressing gown at 11am. This is different from her usual self.

role.q: Who can give Cherry advice about the money worry?
options: a support service such as OPAN

riskind.q: More of Cherry's ornaments could go missing. This is a risk.

abuse.q: What is the sign of possible financial abuse?
options: Ornaments are missing and parcels keep arriving for Donna.

mental.q: Finish Cherry's words: "Now I just want to stay in ________. Talk to ________. Do nothing."

l_selfdet.q: In the report, the support worker tells Lance what Cherry wants and what she decided.

l_policy.q: When do you report possible abuse to your supervisor?

l_mental.q: What the support worker told Lance about Cherry's mental health. Fill in the gaps.

parts.q: One sign of mental ill-health Cherry showed: ________
parts.key: For example: crying, low mood, wants to stay in bed, talk to no one, not eating or sleeping
For example: grief, possible financial abuse, not eating or sleeping, pulling away from people, depends on Donna
For example: her faith and the Minister, the support worker, OPAN, her friends, her strengths

note.q: What belongs in a progress note?
options: Facts, Cherry's own words, what you did and who you told.
A guess about what will happen next.

monitor.q: One thing the class did well, and one thing to do better next time: ________

listen: DO: I sit down next to her and wait quietly.
SAY: "The swan is gone, and it was your favourite." (say back what she said)
SAY: "You sound really sad." (name the feeling)
touch: SAY first: "Would it help if I held your hand?"
DO after she says yes: I hold her hand gently.
esteem: SAY: "You did the right thing telling me."
SAY: "You know the story of every one of these. That's special."
empathy: SAY: "Of course you're upset. They remind you of your Mum."
positive: SAY: "We can work this out together."
prefs: Social, SAY: "Who are your friends? Who do you like to spend time with?"
Cultural, SAY: "Tell me about your family and your traditions."
Spiritual, SAY: "Is your faith important to you?"
respect: SAY: "Your faith matters to you. Let's make sure you can see the Minister."
needs: SAY: "Your hands are shaky today. Would you like me to press the buttons while you talk?"
DO: I bring her walking frame closer.
money: SAY: "What do you think has happened to them?"
Do not say "Did Donna steal them?"
unmet: SAY: "Have you had breakfast today? Did you sleep?"
DO: I make her a cup of tea and some toast.
selfdet: SAY: "What would you like to do?"
pcentred: SAY: "What matters most to you right now?"
SAY: "You have the right to feel safe at home."
risk: SAY: "You don't want to talk to Donna today. That's your choice. Here is some information if you change your mind."
privacy: SAY: "I need to tell my supervisor, Lance. Only people who need to know will be told."
duty: SAY: "I can't keep this a secret, because I need to keep you safe. You will still decide what happens."
SAY: "Do you feel safe at home?"
services: Minister, SAY: "Would you like to ring Reverend Hill for tomorrow? I can help."
Minister, DO: I get the church newsletter from the fridge and press the numbers for her.
Information, DO: I give her an OPAN brochure.
Information, SAY: "OPAN gives free, private advice to older people. You decide what happens."
Dial, DO: Before I leave, I help her dial OPAN on 1800 700 600.
selfmanage: SAY: "Would you like to talk to them yourself?"
DO: I hand her the phone so she can talk.
strengths: SAY: "What has helped you in hard times before?"
selfcare: SAY: "What do you still do for yourself each day?"
SAY: "You still shower and dress yourself. That's great. Keep it up."
values: SAY: "What you do about Donna is your decision."
Do not tell her what she should do.
physical: SAY: "Your hands are shaky and you haven't eaten. How is your body feeling today?"
variation: SAY: "You're usually dressed by now. Today is different. I can see you're not okay."
role: SAY: "Lance, my supervisor, will follow up."
SAY: "OPAN can help with the money worry."
SAY: "Reverend Hill can help with forgiveness."
riskind: SAY: "I'm worried more ornaments could go."
SAY: "Do you feel safe at home?"
abuse: SAY: "Things going missing is a worry. I need to report it so we can support you."
mental: SAY: "You said you want to stay in bed and talk to no one. How are you feeling in yourself?"
SAY: "Are you safe? Are you thinking of hurting yourself?"
l_selfdet: SAY to Lance: "Cherry decided to ring the Minister. She doesn't want the police. It's her choice."
l_policy: SAY to Lance: "Cherry's crystal swan is missing. Only 4 of her 12 animals are left. She thinks her sister Donna is selling them. In her words: ..."
Tell Lance what you saw and what you did.
l_mental: SAY to Lance: "She wants to stay in bed and talk to no one. She hasn't eaten or slept."
Risk factors: grief, not eating, staying away from people, the money worry.
Protective factors: her faith, the Minister, OPAN, you.
note: After the session: write facts, Cherry's own words in quotation marks, what you did, and who you told.
monitor: SAY to Lance: "I think I did well at ... Next time I would ..."
